summary: Mendocino NF lookout built 1935 as a Plan R1 cabin on a rock tower; a later block tower is all that remains, used for communications.

facts.design: USFS Plan R1 cabin first on a 9-foot rock tower; later replaced by a block tower
facts.status_note: Register says only the block tower remains today, used for communications

notes_for_editor: Only the FFLOS register page has content. The Forest Lookouts page for Hunter Point (californialookouts.weebly.com/hunter-point.html) shows a header and no history text, so it is not cited. Two WebSearch calls found no Hunter Point history. A search snippet (Komoot listing, not read) puts a Hunter Point viewpoint in Lake County at 860 m, which does not match the register's Mendocino coordinates; not used. Photo captions only (1943 Upper Lake Ranger District Collection; 2009 Ron Kemnow), no image URLs, so no photos entries. Brief status 'gone' fits the register: the cabin is gone, the block tower remains for communications. Story is short because the evidence is short.
